tasks.short: Review environmental impact report quality and implications

steps.what: Review environmental impact reports, methods, evidence and qualifications
Evaluate environmental report adequacy and request necessary clarification

tasks.design: Keep substantive report review and adequacy judgement with the planner in {DOCS}. The planner checks the exact assessment and clarification requests before handing them to the project lead.
tasks.previous_blocker: A report's completeness and conclusions require scrutiny of methods and assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional component is proposed for report adequacy judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsupported conclusions, missing cumulative effects and limits requiring specialist review.
tasks.human_edge: The planner knows when the report does not answer the planning question despite complete-looking sections.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in substantive review responsibility.

reach.task: Formulate a precise clarification request about study limitations
reach.learn: Study methods and specialist evidence requirements

evidence.claim: Substantive environmental report adequacy review needs contextual judgement; no labour reduction is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is substantive report adequacy review, excluding report production and final proposal approval. Any passage-location work saved in a separate proposal-evaluation task is assigned once, not saved again here.

Existing project specialists produce the report before s1; the planner reads and records observations in s1 and judges adequacy in s2. No new structured adequate-report flag or unpaid specialist recoding is introduced.
Use native document access and review checklists before custom code.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new component or recurring process is added.
research_questions: Which recurring report limitations require specialist clarification rather than faster reading?

already_counted.description: Substantive report reading and adequacy assessment

approvals.approved_version: Exact report version, adequacy assessment, limitations, clarification requests and project lead destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0; substantive report judgement stays human and overlapping retrieval gains are not counted twice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise and coordinate urban planning technical staff

steps.what: Coordinate urban planning technicians' assignments and dependencies
Supervise technical progress, review work and resolve planning questions

tasks.design: Keep assignment decisions, technical supervision and feedback with the planner. Existing work records in {PROJECT} and {DOCS} support discussion without automatic staff assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical work needs clarification, prioritisation and feedback as project conditions change.
tasks.enabler_now: No new component is proposed for contextual supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising quality issues and resolving dependencies without losing staff understanding.
tasks.human_edge: The planner adapts assignments and feedback to the work and the person doing it.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in supervisory authority or time allocation.

reach.task: Coordinate technical dependencies in a joint planning study
reach.learn: Transport work products and review milestones

evidence.claim: Technical supervision depends on contextual prioritisation and feedback; no labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the planner's coordination and supervision, excluding technicians' production work.
Technicians produce work products and progress reports after assignments, before their review in s2, through the existing workflow. No new structured progress feed or extra reporting task is imposed.
Use native project records before any custom build; current dashboard runtime is not a labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because the existing supervision workflow is retained.
research_questions: Which supervision delays reflect unclear assignments or missing decisions?

already_counted.description: Assignment coordination, technical review and feedback

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross and net0; no supervisory or technician time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define transportation alternatives and check their scenario assumptions
Compile transport scenario outputs into comparable tables and maps
Develop public or alternative transportation plans from scenario evidence

tasks.design: Use native scenario comparison tools in the transport modelling system in {OTHER} to compile checked outputs. The planner retains alternative selection, assumptions and plan development, documenting tradeoffs in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scenario outputs are manually copied into comparable views before plan choices can be discussed.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed native exports can align checked scenario identifiers, units and time horizons.
tasks.still_hard: Demand response, model validity, access tradeoffs and whether a plan can be delivered.
tasks.human_edge: The planner tests assumptions and chooses a defensible plan rather than simply selecting the lowest reported emissions.
tasks.altitude: Less scenario-output copying; transport plan choices and interpretation remain human.

reach.task: Prepare a traceable transport alternative comparison
reach.learn: Demand modelling, emissions boundaries and accessibility measures

evidence.claim: PTV Visum is a transport modelling product cited by the digest; its availability does not establish savings for this planner's scenario comparison.
Compiling checked transport scenario outputs with native exports is plausible; the labour estimate is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is the planner's transport alternative specification, comparison and plan development, excluding building a new transport model, implementation and community consultation conducted separately.

OTHER means the existing transport modelling system. The planner produces and checks scenario identifier, model version, geography, horizon, intervention assumptions, demand basis, output fields, units and emissions boundary in s1. Model run selection, output checks and capture remain counted in s1; existing modelling runtime is not labour.

Existing transport model owners maintain the baseline model as current work. The native export produces scenario identifier, measure, value, unit and geography from the checked runs. Missing units or incompatible horizons return to manual comparison in s3, never automatic rescaling or invented emissions factors. Extra model-owner export support is costed below.
Try native comparison reports before custom code. Already automatic scenario comparison receives no new saving; transport and broader sustainability plans must assign shared modelling once.
unknowns: Compatibility of scenario horizons and units
research_questions: Does native comparison reduce total plan preparation time after scenario checks and model support?

already_counted.description: Scenario specification, output checks and contextual plan development

incremental.description: Maintain comparison definitions and inspect sampled output mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R85 gives gross15 and net8 after7 focal upkeep;3 model support hours are visible. Range1-4% assumes repeated manual comparison with an existing model; new modelling and plan judgement earn no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify sustainability opportunities from local conditions and evidence
Develop project choices, delivery assumptions and sustainability tradeoffs
Write sustainability project or programme plan from checked choices

loop.purpose: Express selected project choices in a coherent plan
loop.input: checked project notes with objectives, actions, assumptions and evidence references
loop.check: Verify each proposed action, benefit, delivery assumption and limitation against the planner's chosen approach and evidence
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; planner writes sections with missing decisions manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative project explanations vary, while fixed templates can supply only headings

tasks.design: The planner identifies and chooses sustainability projects, then a bounded step in {DOCS} drafts the plan from checked decisions. The planner verifies wording and assumptions before the draft goes to the programme lead; the model does not select projects or estimate environmental benefits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plan writing repeats the explanation of decisions already made in project development.
tasks.enabler_now: Constrained drafting can express checked project notes without creating a new project or benefit claim.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing feasible interventions and understanding tradeoffs across energy, waste, pollution and natural systems.
tasks.human_edge: The planner connects local conditions and delivery constraints to a defensible project approach.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less plan prose composition; project choice and programme authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a project rationale with explicit evidence limits

evidence.claim: Drafting a sustainability plan from human-selected project choices is plausible; the small task-specific labour reduction is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is opportunity identification, project approach and plan composition, excluding technical study production, formal approval and implementation. Any transport-specific modelling is owned by its task once.

The planner captures objectives, selected actions, evidence references, expected outcome statements, delivery roles, assumptions and limitations during s2; all choice and capture time stays counted. Existing specialists supply their current evidence as normal work, with no new structured benefit calculation or unpaid recoding assumed.
s3 includes full meaning review and manual completion of missing decisions. No automatic quantified environmental saving or project approval is produced.
Try native plan templates before a model step; existing document runtime earns no labour saving.
research_questions: Does plan drafting save time after checking project assumptions and correcting unsupported benefits?

already_counted.description: Opportunity identification, project choice and checked-note capture

incremental.description: Maintain plan examples and inspect unsupported-benefit errors

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R91.25 gives gross8.75 and net2.75 after6 upkeep. Range0-1% assumes some reusable plan prose while allowing substantial correction; project choice and evidence production remain unchanged.
